panels.title: POST /auth/login p95 from client
panels.description: Measured by the traffic generator from request execution through Gateway until the response body is consumed or the request fails/times out. Includes client/network time and both services. Setup and token renewal are excluded. Dropped arrivals are not timed; a missing series is not zero latency.

panels.title: GET /users/me p95 from client
panels.description: Measured by the traffic generator for GET /api/identity/users/me through Gateway until the response body is consumed or the request fails/times out. Identity handles GET /users/me. The separate scale makes millisecond changes visible. Setup, token renewal, and dropped arrivals are excluded.

panels.title: Client offered load and completed requests
panels.description: Traffic-generator accounting: offered arrivals include requests the generator drops; completed requests include successful responses and failures/timeouts. The workload changes its login share while retaining the same total offered rate. Completion can lag admission when requests slow or remain in flight. Compare this with server route rates to distinguish the workload from observed throughput.

panels.title: POST /auth/login p95 at Gateway and Identity
panels.description: Compare route duration at each server boundary. These are separate p95 populations, not an exact decomposition of one request; use a trace exemplar for that.

panels.title: GET /users/me p95 at Gateway and Identity
panels.description: Compare the lightweight route at both server boundaries on its own scale. Open a same-period trace to locate any gap.

panels.title: Recent Identity POST /auth/login traces
panels.description: Login traces in the selected time range. Open a trace to compare Gateway, Identity, SQL, and authentication work. The most recent trace is not necessarily the p95 request.

panels.title: Recent Identity GET /users/me traces
panels.description: Lightweight control requests in the selected time range. Compare a trace from the same period as a slow login and inspect Gateway, Identity, and SQL spans.

panels.title: Password verification and permit wait p95
panels.description: Argon2 verification and its permit wait contribute to login time. Verification runs on the blocking pool with four permits; compare its duration with the synchronous check and scheduler delay. The verification histogram includes permit wait. No credential or user identifier is exported.

panels.title: Synchronous authentication check p95
panels.description: The simulated third-party check waits on a thread after credentials are verified. Its duration includes the four-permit wait; compare it with the login trace and scheduler delay.

panels.title: Identity Cats Effect scheduler signals
panels.description: One line per signal across rebuilds: maximum scheduler drift and total starvation events in the selected window. Retained gauge values from retired instances are excluded after the metric window clears. Drift uses the left axis in milliseconds; events use the right axis. Missing telemetry does not prove recovery.

panels.title: Password verifications holding permits
panels.description: Total password verifications holding permits across active instances. Each Identity instance allows up to four concurrent verifications. Retained values from retired instances are excluded after the metric window clears.

options.content: Confirm the report in the **p95 from client** panels (traffic-generator measurements) and note when the offered login mix changed. Compare Gateway with Identity for each route. Open a login trace from the tables above and inspect SQL, `identity.password.permit.wait`, `identity.password.verify.work`, and `identity.login.legacy_check`; then compare a `GET /users/me` trace from the same period. Compare the synchronous check duration, password verification, and permit wait with scheduler delay. The check retains its 250 ms wait after repair; verify recovery of the lightweight route under the same mix. Use offered and completed rates plus active password verifications to assess the workload. Check drops in Workshop Traffic when validating a comparison. Recovery means responsive GET /users/me and lower scheduler delay at the same offered mix. Exclude startup and rollout intervals before judging recovery. Successful response-body measurements may lack exemplars, so use the trace tables when no diamond appears. Missing telemetry during saturation does not prove recovery.
